claims.text: The target material is bulk HfNbTaTiZr containing 1 wt.% oxygen.

A model incorporating explicit defect interactions, anharmonic lattice dynamics, and temperature-dependent phonon scattering will outperform earlier methods for predicting lattice thermal conductivity.
The proposed model is applicable from 50 K to 1200 K.
The model is expected to provide particular improvement below 200 K and above 300 K.
Lattice and electronic thermal-transport contributions are significant in the specified low- and high-temperature regimes.
Oxygen impurities influence thermal transport in HfNbTaTiZr.
Defect interactions and anharmonic lattice dynamics affect phonon scattering.
Capturing defects, anharmonicity, and temperature-dependent scattering improves the accuracy of phonon-transport predictions.
Earlier analytical or DFT-based methods do not fully capture the relevant atomic-scale complexity.
The proposed model will predict lattice thermal conductivity within 10% of experiment throughout 50–1200 K.
Earlier methods deviate from experimental thermal-conductivity data by more than 20%.
The approach is limited to bulk HfNbTaTiZr with impurity levels similar to 1 wt.% oxygen.
The approach does not apply to nanostructured or highly defective samples.
Variations in impurity distribution and inaccuracies in anharmonic-interaction modeling can introduce prediction uncertainty, especially at extreme temperatures.
The hypothesis is falsified if the proposed model exceeds 10% error over the stated range or if an earlier method has comparable or better accuracy.
